assertions.text: Before costs, the return on the average actively managed dollar equals the return on the average passively managed dollar.
The market return over a period is the value-weighted average of the returns on the securities in the market, so a passive holder earns precisely it before costs.

After costs, the average actively managed dollar returns less than the average passively managed dollar. The source asserts this alongside the before-costs equality but derives only the equality; the inequality additionally requires that active management costs more.
The result rests on a single source and one deductive chain, not on independent replication.

summary: Given exhaustive definitions of active and passive management, the return on the average actively managed dollar equals the market return before costs and falls below the passive return after costs. The result is an accounting identity that holds over any period and depends only on arithmetic, so it is not contingent on market conditions or on any claim about manager skill.
title: Arithmetic of active management: active and passive dollars earn the market return before costs
